evidence.claim: Buhari said section 84(12) conflicted with the constitution and asked the National Assembly to amend the bill by deleting that section.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the Signing of Electoral Bill 2022
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said section 84(12) conflicted with the constitution and asked the National Assembly to amend the bill by deleting that section.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit language about the requested amendment and legal rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari action; this shows an executive attempt to change the rules around political appointee participation.
contrary_evidence: He still assented to the broader reform package
the legislature later refused to follow his amendment request

evidence.claim: The mission said the 2022 Electoral Act enjoyed wide stakeholder support and improved INEC's ability to deliver more transparent elections through clearer timelines, technology, and earlier funding.
evidence.title: Statement of the First Joint NDI/IRI Pre-Election Assessment Mission to Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: The mission said the 2022 Electoral Act enjoyed wide stakeholder support and improved INEC's ability to deliver more transparent elections through clearer timelines, technology, and earlier funding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent election-observation mission after meetings with INEC, National Assembly, parties, civil society, media, security forces, and diplomats.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material because Buhari assented to the law and its early effects were under his administration.
contrary_evidence: The mission warned full implementation was uncertain
INEC was not yet fully funded by the government as mandated by law

evidence.claim: The mission said women, youth, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons still faced major barriers to political participation, even though some parties had reduced nomination fees and added marginalized delegates.
evidence.title: Statement of the First Joint NDI/IRI Pre-Election Assessment Mission to Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: The mission said women, youth, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons still faced major barriers to political participation, even though some parties had reduced nomination fees and added marginalized delegates.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent mission report with specific findings on candidate access and inclusion gaps.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; this describes the political environment Buhari governed rather than a single presidential order.
contrary_evidence: Some parties reduced fees for women aspirants
APC and PDP added women/PWD delegates

evidence.claim: The Senate rejected President Buhari's executive request to amend the 2022 Electoral Act and refused to proceed while the matter was subject to a court order and due process concerns.
evidence.title: Senate rejects amendment to Electoral Act 2022
evidence.publisher: National Assembly of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: The Senate rejected President Buhari's executive request to amend the 2022 Electoral Act and refused to proceed while the matter was subject to a court order and due process concerns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary record of the vote and the stated legal rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important as a constraint on Buhari's preferred rule change, not a presidential act itself.
contrary_evidence: The request itself came from Buhari
the legislature, not the president, stopped the amendment

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari gave cabinet members a deadline to resign before seeking office, and ten ministers had already resigned to comply.
evidence.title: Four Nigerian ministers drop election bid to remain in cabinet
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari gave cabinet members a deadline to resign before seeking office, and ten ministers had already resigned to comply.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct, contemporaneous attribution and concrete cabinet compliance details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari executive action through cabinet rules.
contrary_evidence: This also shows incumbents using state office while transitioning
four ministers initially stayed despite the deadline

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari was constitutionally barred from contesting and had no preferred successor from the ruling party.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari was constitutionally barred from contesting and had no preferred successor from the ruling party.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report reproduced by Al Jazeera with direct quotes and a clear date.
contrary_evidence: The ruling party still had internal succession struggles
lack of a preferred successor does not itself prove full neutrality

evidence.claim: CPJ reported that Nigerian police arrested Agba Jalingo in August 2022 over a defamation and cyberattack complaint, moved him through multiple detention sites, and urged authorities to stop harassing him.
evidence.title: Nigerian journalist Agba Jalingo detained over defamation, cyberattack complaint
evidence.excerpt: CPJ reported that Nigerian police arrested Agba Jalingo in August 2022 over a defamation and cyberattack complaint, moved him through multiple detention sites, and urged authorities to stop harassing him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous alert with named officials, complaint, and custody trail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; this reflects policing under Buhari's administration, though the complaint came from a state governor's circle.
contrary_evidence: State-level complaint rather than a federal directive
authorities said it was a response to defamation/cybercrime allegations

evidence.claim: Amnesty said that more than 40 #EndSARS protesters were still in prison in October 2022, while the panels set up to investigate police impunity had failed to deliver justice and peaceful protest continued to face threats and intimidation.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Two years on, more than 40 #EndSARS protesters still languishing in jail
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said that more than 40 #EndSARS protesters were still in prison in October 2022, while the panels set up to investigate police impunity had failed to deliver justice and peaceful protest continued to face threats and intimidation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights report with named detention patterns, remedy failures, and protest-treatment allegations.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022, with continuing effects from 2020 protests.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important; the detention and failure of remedy persisted under Buhari's government.
contrary_evidence: The arrests originated in 2020
this is advocacy reporting on continuing detention, not a new Buhari order in 2022

evidence.claim: The ECOWAS Court ruled that Nigeria's Twitter ban was unlawful and said the Buhari administration must not repeat it.
evidence.title: Twitter ban in Nigeria unlawful, ECOWAS court rules
evidence.excerpt: The ECOWAS Court ruled that Nigeria's Twitter ban was unlawful and said the Buhari administration must not repeat it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable local media report of a regional court ruling with a clear legal outcome and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to the Buhari administration, though the ruling itself was issued by a regional court.
contrary_evidence: The case challenged a prior 2021 ban
this is a legal check after the fact rather than a presidential decision

evidence.claim: CDD's preliminary Osun report found BVAS in almost all polling units, 92 percent of observed units had critical materials, and INEC's mock accreditation appeared to work.
evidence.title: Osun election: CDD observe compliance with BVAS, violation of electoral act
evidence.excerpt: CDD's preliminary Osun report found BVAS in almost all polling units, 92 percent of observed units had critical materials, and INEC's mock accreditation appeared to work.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local observer report quoted in a reputable newspaper with concrete numerical findings.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 off-cycle election under the new Electoral Act.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; it supports the claim that Buhari's 2022 reforms had some operational effect, but INEC and state actors ran the election.
contrary_evidence: Some polling units still lacked BVAS
the same report noted electoral-act violations

evidence.claim: The same CDD report said party agents campaigned near polling units in 14 LGAs and fact-checkers tracked misinformation and misleading claims aimed at voters.
evidence.title: Osun election: CDD observe compliance with BVAS, violation of electoral act
evidence.excerpt: The same CDD report said party agents campaigned near polling units in 14 LGAs and fact-checkers tracked misinformation and misleading claims aimed at voters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same observer report with detailed local violations and misinformation monitoring.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; this reflects the electoral environment under Buhari's final year rather than a direct presidential act.
contrary_evidence: Violations were by party agents rather than Buhari personally
the same report also found substantial BVAS compliance

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice under Buhari's own authority
Independent corroboration of the HEU-to-LEU conversion and other nuclear-security claims
Independent evidence of actual conflict-management effect from Buhari's Ukraine/ECOWAS diplomacy
Direct documentary support for the contested Lake Chad weapons claim or any concrete cross-border security outcome
More precise chain-of-command and federal-versus-state attribution for abuses and remedies
More direct evidence on Buhari's personal role in media and protest restrictions, beyond security-service and state-level actions
Independent implementation evidence for the 2022 Electoral Act and related reforms
More household-level and distributional evidence on the effects of subsidy, naira redesign, and fiscal choices
Cleaner evidence on whether economic appointees were selected for competence versus loyalty
Independent outcome evaluation of school feeding, BHCPF, rotavirus rollout, and related social programs
Subnational delivery and attribution, especially for north-south and rural-urban differences
Direct evidence on assets, beneficial ownership, gifts, campaign finance, or family enrichment
More independent evidence on truthfulness, correction, and acceptance of scrutiny
Better separation of Buhari's personal conduct from broader authoritarian or state-level behavior
Audited completion data for major projects and service-delivery claims
Independent evidence that coordination bodies and new appointments changed implementation quality
